subject: Microvendor auto-approval criteria & escalation flow
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: QuickShip Procurement <procure@quickship.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Microvendor auto-approval criteria & escalation flow

Team —

Following last week's ops sync, I sketched a short proposal for a low-friction onboarding path for "microvendors" (small suppliers frequently used by engineering and ops teams). Goal: let product teams spin up trial integrations quickly while keeping procurement controls in place. High-level rules I propose (attached as spreadsheet):

- Threshold: vendors with expected spend <= $2,000/month or $20,000/year.
- Required intake steps: vendor portal registration, completed onboarding form, valid W-9 (or equivalent), and payment routing verified.
- Risk screening: basic sanctions check + manual review if vendor requests data access beyond metadata. No SOC2 for microvendors; escalate if data access scope expands.
- Auto-approval: if all required intake steps done and no red flags in screening, system auto-approves and routes invoices to AP with "invoice-only" processing (no PO required).
- Escalation: any missing docs, failed screening, or spend forecast > threshold triggers an automatic 1st-level review by Procurement. For exceptions, use the attached escalation_matrix_v1.pdf.

Attachments: microvendor_auto_criteria.xlsx (criteria table), escalation_matrix_v1.pdf (who to loop + SLAs).

Ask: Marissa/Monica — can you review the intake checklist and confirm whether the "invoice-only" path needs any legal covering language? Karthik — can procurement confirm we can operationalize auto-approval flags in the vendor portal?

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Microvendor auto-approval criteria & escalation flow

Rishi —

Thanks for the clear draft. Quick notes inline and next steps: 

- Threshold: I'm okay with $2k/month for most services (SaaS, integrations). For vendors that handle PII or payment processing, bump threshold to $500/month and require Procurement sign-off.
- Invoice-only: AP needs a short clause in the intake form that the vendor acknowledges invoices may be processed without a PO under the microvendor program. Legal should draft a one-sentence clause; we can include it as part of the portal onboarding.
- Evidence: rather than W-9 only, require either W-9 or foreign equivalent + confirmation of bank details (ACH test or voided check).

Action items:
1) Monica — please loop Legal for the one-line invoice-only acknowledgement.
2) Karthik — can Procurement add a flag in the vendor portal for "handles_sensitive_data" so those vendors don't auto-approve?
3) Rishi — if you can update the spreadsheet with these fields, I'll run it by Sales Ops for practical edge-cases.

On the escalation SLAs — 24h for 1st-level review, 72h for full exception decision seems reasonable.

—Marissa
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

From: QuickShip Procurement <procure@quickship.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Microvendor auto-approval criteria & escalation flow

Hi Rishi / team —

Appreciate the proposal. QuickShip is piloting with a few vendors that would benefit from a no-PO path. Two clarifying questions from our side: 

1) How will invoices be routed to AP without a PO? Do we need to include a unique vendor reference or invoice header to make reconciliation straightforward on our side?
2) If the vendor becomes eligible for higher spend later, what's the notification cadence? We need to avoid surprise overruns.

Proposed reconciliation field: include Vendor Portal ID + Redwood Account ID on every invoice; that should let us auto-match invoices. For spend changes, an automated monthly alert from the portal when a vendor's rolling 30-day spend exceeds 75% of the threshold.

Happy to join a quick 30-min call to align.

Best,
Ava Lin
Vendor Ops Manager
QuickShip Logistics

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, QuickShip Procurement <procure@quickship.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Microvendor auto-approval criteria & escalation flow

Thanks, everyone — good feedback. Short summary and owners: 

- Policy: adopt auto-approve path for microvendors (<= $2k/mo) except where vendor handles sensitive data. (Marissa: finalize spend exceptions list)
- Intake: require portal registration, W-9/foreign equivalent, bank verification, and invoice header with Vendor Portal ID + Redwood Account ID. (Monica: add the required fields to the intake form and coordinate Legal for the one-line invoice acknowledgement)
- Portal flags & alerts: add "handles_sensitive_data" flag and a rolling-spend monitor that alerts at 75% threshold. (Karthik: prod ticket to add flags + PROC-8921 is the Jira)
- Escalation SLAs: 24h 1st-level, 72h final decision. (Procurement to staff appropriately for the pilot window.)
- Next step: schedule a 30-min alignment call with QuickShip (Ava) tomorrow morning; I'll send a calendar invite once Marissa confirms the final threshold.

Attachments referenced: microvendor_auto_criteria.xlsx, escalation_matrix_v1.pdf (see folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cEXAMPLE).

Thanks again — I'll follow up with the calendar invite and updated spreadsheet.

Rishi
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment stubs:
- microvendor_auto_criteria.xlsx (spreadsheet, 5 rows of vendor type examples + columns: threshold, required_docs, portal_fields)
- escalation_matrix_v1.pdf (PDF, 2 pages: review owners + SLA table)
